episode_summary: Episode 383, recorded in early 2022, with Dee and Jesse catching up with guest Corey Petty. The conversation covers NFTs and play-to-earn games (Avalanche chickens, Axie Infinity scholarships), the middleman problem, skepticism about USDC, Tether, HEX and Luna, India's tax treatment of crypto, the threat of government bans and CBDCs, and Helium's wireless network. It closes with the planned move to Hashing It Out and the DAD DAO built on Algorand.

cards.claim: One speaker said the largest and still sustainable threat to crypto is that governments will ban it, with central bank digital currency the hardest existential threat.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: the largest and still sustainable threat to crypto is that governments will ban it.

cards.claim: One speaker argued that a government ban makes crypto harder to access in that jurisdiction but does not kill a globally dispersed asset, pointing to China.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: But just because a given jurisdiction makes it more difficult to access a globally dispersed asset doesn't kill it.

cards.claim: The hosts said India had gone from banning bitcoin to making it legal, but applies a 30 percent VAT-style tax when crypto is spent.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: they're applying a 30 percent vat tax when you spend it

cards.claim: One speaker questioned how USDC, a stablecoin, could rank in the top 10 crypto assets by market cap, saying it did not make sense.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: How does it even make sense that USDC is in the top 10 and USDC is just a stable coin?

cards.claim: One speaker predicted that the Tether bomb, a Tether collapse, would become the biggest crypto myth that never materializes.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: I think the Tether Bomb is going to be something in crypto that is like the biggest myth that never materializes

cards.claim: One speaker predicted Tether would not implode because too many very wealthy people hold its money and would not let it fail.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: the reason why usdt is not going to implode is because too many really really wealthy people have money so they're not going to let it implode period

cards.claim: The hosts debated HEX: one called it a garbage, well-made Ponzi that only funnels money to Richard Heart, while another argued the Ponzi label misses nuance in how its value rises.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: hex is garbage it's it's the best made ponzi and all ponzi that have ever ponzi

cards.claim: One speaker said HEX is a single point of failure in Richard Heart, and suggested a clone without his primary account would be interesting.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: but he is a complete single point of failure.

cards.claim: One speaker defined a Ponzi scheme as making money by getting other people to put money in, and the hosts debated whether that also describes an MLM.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: Ponzi is I make money by getting other people to put money in.

cards.claim: The hosts explained that Axie Infinity already has middlemen who issue 'scholarships', letting players use their accounts in exchange for a share of earnings.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: the concept of middlemen already exists in the way that there are people

cards.claim: Corey said that the more inclusive and generalized a platform is, the more likely it is to attract scammers, fraud and pyramid schemes.
cards.speaker: Corey
cards.quote: the more inclusive and generalized of a platform you create the more likely there is to be scammers, fraud, pyramid schemes

cards.claim: One speaker said pay-to-earn is turning into microloans, which can help a community or hurt it depending on the system.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: I think pay to earn is turning into microloans.

cards.claim: One speaker predicted that crypto businesses will always be middlemen, because most people will pay someone else to manage their assets.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: We're going to be middlemen, bro. There's no way around it.

cards.claim: One speaker said most top-20 tokens have serious technical problems, and that the market would catch up with that in time.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: From a technical perspective, there's serious problems with the majority of the top 20 tokens.

cards.claim: One speaker said Avalanche is one of the most novel projects in the ecosystem and has potential to scale.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: Avalanche is, in my opinion, one of the most novel projects in the entire ecosystem that has potential to scale.

cards.claim: The hosts said Helium node operators earn more return on investment in elevated rural areas, and the first node in a location gets the most.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: You actually get more ROI if you're the first node.

cards.claim: The hosts described Helium's initial network as low-bandwidth, long-range LoRa coverage for IoT devices, not Wi-Fi for phones.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: It's a low bandwidth, long range coverage for IoT devices. Not for your phone connecting to Wi-Fi.

cards.claim: In early 2022 the hosts announced the Bitcoin Podcast was moving over to a new show called Hashing It Out, with no migration details yet.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: everything's moving over to hashing it out we have no details as to what that migration looks like

cards.claim: The hosts said they were building a DAO on Algorand, with a Discord gated by holding a specific Algorand asset.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: We're actually trying to build a distributed autonomous organization on top of Algorand

cards.claim: One speaker said Solana is really crappy and that its good performance rests on a strong marketing team and branding.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: I think Solana is really crappy. It's good at one thing, but it's got a really good marketing team behind it

cards.claim: The hosts said the US Congress was already framing USDC as something the government would one day take over.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: the u.s congress has already started to paint the picture in verbiage that one day they're just going to take usdc

cards.claim: Corey said he bought his wife an Avalanche chicken NFT, and the chicken game's egg and feed token mechanics were too hard for his family to understand.
cards.speaker: Corey
cards.quote: the concept of the avalanche chickens came up because i bought my wife a chicken

cards.claim: Corey said the Chicken NFT was the first real NFT project that caught his eye, though not because it does anything phenomenal.
cards.speaker: Corey
cards.quote: it's the first real nft project that caught my eye

title: The Bitcoin Podcast #383- ByThe Power of the Executive Order
